title: Sky School · How fast are you moving?

post.title: You are not sitting still 🚀
post.description:
Even sitting still in central Europe, Earth's spin carries you at about 1,076 km/h, Earth's orbit at about 107,000 km/h (29.8 km/s), and the Sun carries us around the Milky Way at about 720,000 km/h. Each speed is measured relative to a different centre.

Sources:
NASA NSSDCA Planetary Fact Sheet: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/
NASA NSSDCA Earth Fact Sheet: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
NASA Science, Sun facts: https://science.nasa.gov/sun/facts/

Images: NASA / JSC (Blue Marble), NASA / JPL-Caltech (Spitzer). Narration uses a synthetic voice.

narration: Even sitting perfectly still, you are flying through space.
Right now, you are moving in several ways at once.
In central Europe, that carries you east at about 1,076 kilometres an hour.

params.label: Earth's spin, in central Europe (50° N)
params.sourceLine: Computed from NASA's Earth fact sheet

narration: Second, Earth circles the Sun at 29.8 kilometres every second.
That is about 107,000 kilometres an hour, a hundred times faster.
Third, the Sun carries all of us around the centre of the Milky Way, at about 720,000 kilometres an hour.
Even so, one lap takes about 230 million years.
Side by side, the spin that gives us day and night is barely a sliver.
